BiblicalUsage: Chaliyphah means a change — of raiment, of shifts, of turns. Joseph gave each brother changes of raiment and Benjamin five, Samson wagered thirty changes of garments on his riddle, Solomon sent ten thousand men a month to Lebanon by courses, and Naaman carried ten changes of raiment to the king of Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe changes of clothing are changes of fortune in this word: Joseph's gift, Samson's wager, Solomon's courses, and Naaman's payment. God changes the garments of His people, and He changes their fortunes with them.
RelatedPeople: Joseph, Son of Jacob; Samson; King Solomon
RelatedEvents: Joseph and His Brothers; Naaman Healed of Leprosy
